summary:
BREATHEAI is an innovative, non-invasive smart breath-analysis device and AI-driven software solution designed to safeguard astronaut health during deep-space missions.

Inspired by NASA Glenn Research Center and Cleveland Clinic’s pioneering gas-sensing research, we developed a compact, low-cost diagnostic system powered by a Esp-32 microcontroller, a specialized semiconductor gas sensor array, and a K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) machine learning model built in Python. By capturing a single exhalation, BREATHEAI detects real-time shifts in Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs)—specifically ethane and pentane—to identify radiation-induced oxidative/metabolic stress alongside chemical markers linked to chronic depression and isolation.

Directly addressing the Space Apps challenge, BREATHEAI replaces bulky, invasive blood and urine lab equipment with an autonomous, offline, zero-gravity-compatible diagnostic tool. As humanity prepares for long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars where communication delays prevent real-time Earth-based medical intervention, BREATHEAI empowers astronauts with instant, actionable health insights in seconds—protecting both their physical resilience and mental well-being millions of miles from home.
details:
BREATHEAI is an autonomous, non-invasive smart breath-analysis device and AI-driven health monitoring platform engineered to protect astronauts during deep-space missions. By analyzing volatile biomarkers in a single exhalation, it detects early chemical signs of radiation-induced oxidative/metabolic stress and chronic depression—eliminating the need for invasive blood draws or complex lab equipment in microgravity.

1. What It Does & How It Works

BREATHEAI captures an astronaut’s exhaled breath through a compact mouthpiece routed into a sealed sensor chamber. Inside, a specialized array of semiconductor gas sensors measures real-time concentration shifts in specific Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs):

  • Ethane & Pentane: Key hydrocarbon byproducts of lipid peroxidation, serving as immediate biomarkers for cellular damage and oxidative/metabolic stress caused by cosmic radiation.
  • Stress & Mood-Related VOCs (e.g., Acetone, Isoprene, and Ammonia shifts): Chemical patterns linked to metabolic dysregulation, sleep disruption, and chronic depression/isolation.

Once captured, the raw sensor signals undergo noise filtering and baseline calibration (compensating for breath humidity and cabin temperature) before being fed into a K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) machine learning model. The model compares the astronaut’s live "breath print" against baseline healthy profiles to deliver an instant risk assessment and diagnostic readout directly on the device interface.

2. Key Benefits

  • 100% Non-Invasive & Painless: Requires only a simple breath sample, avoiding the hazards of needle sticks and floating bio-fluids in zero gravity.
  • Instant, Real-Time Results: Delivers diagnostic insights within seconds, replacing traditional workflows where blood or urine samples must be frozen and returned to Earth months later for mass spectrometry analysis.
  • Offline & Autonomous Operation: Runs locally without relying on continuous Earth communication—critical for Moon and Mars missions where signal latency can reach up to 20 minutes.
  • Lightweight & Cost-Effective: Dramatically reduces payload mass, volume, and power consumption compared to conventional spaceflight medical hardware.

3. Intended Impact

  • In Space Exploration: Empowers astronauts with proactive, self-administered health monitoring on long-duration missions, allowing early intervention (such as antioxidant protocols, dietary adjustments, or psychological support) before silent cellular or neurological stress escalates into mission-critical illness.
  • On Earth (Dual-Use Potential): Provides an affordable, portable screening tool for remote clinics, developing regions, and home healthcare to monitor metabolic disorders, oxidative stress, and mental health indicators without expensive lab infrastructure.

4. Tools, Hardware, Software & Languages Used

  • Hardware & Microcontroller: Cyber Pi main control unit for sensor interfacing, edge data acquisition, and local user interface display, paired with a custom Semiconductor / Metal-Oxide Gas Sensor Array (Science Sensor suite) targeted at VOCs, ethane, and pentane detection.
  • Programming Language: Python for data preprocessing, signal normalization, feature extraction, and model deployment.
  • Machine Learning & Software: Scikit-learn (implementing the KNN classification algorithm), NumPy and Pandas for multi-dimensional sensor vector processing, and NASA Open Data / NTRS research literature (specifically NASA Glenn Research Center and Cleveland Clinic gas-sensing studies) to benchmark target biomarkers and sensor behavior.

5. How BREATHEAI Is Creative

  • Replacing Hardware Complexity with Algorithmic Intelligence: Traditional NASA and Cleveland Clinic breath-analysis prototypes relied on expensive, high-temperature Silicon Carbide (SiC) microfabricated sensors to isolate single gases. BREATHEAI takes a creative software-first approach: it uses accessible, low-cost commercial semiconductor sensors and compensates for cross-sensitivity by training a KNN pattern-recognition model to read the holistic chemical signature of multiple gases simultaneously.
  • Targeted Dual-Focus for Space: Rather than building a generic air-quality monitor, BREATHEAI specifically bridges physical radiation biology (lipid peroxidation) and space psychology (isolation-induced depression) into a single unified breath-diagnostic workflow.

6. Key Factors Considered by the Team

  • Microgravity Compatibility: Ensuring the system relies purely on gas-phase airflow rather than gravity-dependent fluid separation.
  • Environmental & Cross-Sensitivity Interference: Accounting for high breath humidity, cabin temperature fluctuations, and background spacecraft air contaminants during signal preprocessing.
  • Communication Latency & Edge Computing: Designing the ML model to be lightweight enough to run locally on edge hardware with zero cloud dependency.
  • Astronaut Usability & Payload Constraints: Minimizing device footprint, power draw, and testing time so daily health checks seamlessly fit into an astronaut’s tightly scheduled routine.
